title: Composition and two-out-of-six for Dwyer--Kan equivalences of Segal spaces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, homotopy fibers and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and the Reedy model structure of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A simplicial space is a functor $V:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$. It is a Segal space if it is Reedy fibrant and its consecutive-edge maps $V_n\to V_1\times_{V_0}\cdots\times_{V_0}V_1$ are weak homotopy equivalences for every $n\geq2$. For vertices $x,y$ of $V_0$, let $M_V(x,y)$ be the strict fiber of $(d_1,d_0):V_1\to V_0^2$. The homotopy category $hV$ has those vertices as objects, morphisms $\pi_0M_V(x,y)$, identity from $s_0$, and composition from the degree-two Segal map and $d_1$.

Call a map $t:A\to B$ of Segal spaces a Dwyer--Kan equivalence if $ht:hA\to hB$ is an equivalence of ordinary categories and $M_A(x,y)\to M_B(tx,ty)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every pair of vertices $x,y$ of $A_0$.

Let $A_0,A_1,A_2,A_3$ be small Segal spaces. For composable maps $a:A_0\to A_1$ and $b:A_1\to A_2$, if $a,b$ are Dwyer--Kan equivalences, then so is $b\circ a$. For composable maps $a:A_0\to A_1$, $b:A_1\to A_2$ and $c:A_2\to A_3$, if $b\circ a$ and $c\circ b$ are Dwyer--Kan equivalences, then each of $a,b,c$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. No completeness assumption on any $A_i$ is imposed.

source.place: Section 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, printed p. 16. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this Segal-space theorem.

proof.text: First prove the composition clause. On homotopy categories, quasi-inverses for $ha$ and $hb$, in reverse order, give a quasi-inverse for $h(b a)=(hb)(ha)$; whiskering the two given natural isomorphisms gives the inverse equations. At a pair $x,y$ of objects of $A_0$, the actual map on strict mapping fibers for $b a$ is the composite of the maps for $a$ at $(x,y)$ and $b$ at $(ax,ay)$. Both are weak equivalences. The Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], with the model-category two-out-of-three axiom stated in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], makes their composite a weak equivalence. This proves the first clause directly.

source.place: Section 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, first clause (printed p.16).

proof.text:
We prepare explicit mapping-space operations for the cancellation clause. Fix any of the Segal spaces $V$. For a finite simplicial subset $L$ of an outer simplex, write $V(L)_q$ for compatible assignments of elements of $V_{k,q}$ to its $k$-simplices. Restriction along $L\subseteq L'$ is a Kan fibration: attach the finitely many missing nondegenerate simplices in increasing dimension. At a $k$-simplex the restriction is a pullback of $V_k\to M_kV$, which is a Kan fibration by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Pullbacks and composites have the horn-lifting property, by pulling a lifting square back, or lifting it successively. The same argument with the vertex subset gives $V_n\to V_0^{n+1}$ a Kan fibration; $V_0$ and its finite powers are Kan, filling horns coordinatewise. Thus its strict fibers $V(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ are Kan. Restriction to the spine gives the Segal map, hence a Kan fibration and a weak equivalence. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] it has the boundary-lifting property, as does its pullback
$$q_n:V(x_0,\ldots,x_n)\longrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^n M_V(x_{i-1},x_i).$$
In particular all the mapping spaces used below are Kan. Boundary lifting extends to lifting against every monomorphism: express that monomorphism as the transfinite boundary-cell composite supplied by the same node, choose lifts at successor stages and take their compatible union at limit stages. Consequently $q_n$ has a section $s_n$ (lift the identity of its target against the empty inclusion). If $u,v:P\to V(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ are two lifts of the same $P\to\prod_iM_V(x_{i-1},x_i)$, lift along $P\times\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow P\times\Delta^1$, with that base map constant in the interval, to obtain a simplicial homotopy from $u$ to $v$ over the target. This is a parameterized lifting argument, not only a statement about components.

source.place: Sections 4.1 and 5.1 (printed pp.11-12), boundary-lifting expansion of the stated trivial fibrations.

proof.text: Choose such sections for $n=2,3$ and every object tuple. Define $\mu_V(v,u)=d_1s_2(u,v)$. These operations are associative and unital up to homotopies of maps of the entire mapping spaces, as follows. On triples $(u,v,w)$ let $t=s_3(u,v,w)$. Its faces $d_3t,d_1t$ calculate $w\circ(v\circ u)$, while $d_0t,d_2t$ calculate $(w\circ v)\circ u$. Compare $d_3t$ with the chosen lift $s_2(u,v)$ over the same pair using the lift homotopy in step 2, and then compare $d_1t$ with the chosen lift of $(d_1d_3t,w)$; these comparisons homotope the first parenthesization to $d_1d_1t$. Similarly the other parenthesization is homotopic to $d_1d_2t$. The equality $d_1d_1=d_1d_2$ identifies their endpoints. For the units, compare $s_2(1,u)$ and $s_2(u,1)$ with $s_0u$ and $s_1u$ respectively; the identities $d_1s_0=d_1s_1=1$ give the unit homotopies. All comparisons use the boundary-lifting consequence of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] as in step 2, with the parameter space retained. For a map $f:V\to V'$, the two maps $f_2s_2$ and $s'_2(f_1\times f_1)$ into $V'(fx,fy,fz)$ lift the same pair in the target of $q'_2$, so the same argument gives $f\mu_V\simeq\mu_{V'}(f\times f)$. Identities are preserved strictly. Passing to components proves functoriality of the specified $hV$ and shows that these composition operations give precisely its stated composition.

source.place: Sections 5.3-5.5 and Proposition 5.4 (printed pp.12-13), with the same lift argument performed on parameter spaces.

proof.text:
If $\alpha:x\to x'$ and $\beta:y\to y'$ represent isomorphisms in $hV$, choose arrows $\bar\alpha:x'\to x$, $\bar\beta:y'\to y$ representing their inverses. The equations in $hV$ say that the four composites lie in the components of the corresponding identities in the Kan mapping spaces. Points in the same component are joined by a finite chain of simplicial edges: partition the vertices by the equivalence relation generated by edge endpoints. Every simplex has all its vertices in one class. These labels define a continuous map from the quotient realization to the discrete set of classes, and each fiber is path connected, since a point of a simplex joins a vertex by a straight line and vertices in one class join by finitely many realized edges. Thus these classes are exactly the path components. Compose those edges with $\mu_V$ and use the parameterized associativity and unit homotopies of step 3. This proves that
$$T_V:M_V(x,y)\longrightarrow M_V(x',y'),\qquad u\longmapsto\beta\circ u\circ\bar\alpha$$
has homotopy inverse $u'\mapsto\bar\beta\circ u'\circ\alpha$, after realization. Indeed the composites reassociate to $(\bar\beta\beta)u(\bar\alpha\alpha)$ and $(\beta\bar\beta)u'(\alpha\bar\alpha)$ and then to $u,u'$. The cylinder homeomorphism of [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] turns every simplicial homotopy here into a continuous homotopy with the same endpoints; finite chains concatenate as continuous homotopies. The homotopy-equivalence clause of [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change] therefore makes $T_V$ a weak homotopy equivalence, including at nonstationary basepoints. By the naturality in step 3, for $f:V\to V'$ the square with horizontal maps $T_V,T_{V'}$, using $f\alpha,f\beta$ and their specified inverse representatives in $V'$, and vertical maps on mapping spaces induced by $f$, commutes up to such a homotopy. Thus a mapping-space map for $f$ is a weak equivalence at $(x,y)$ if and only if it is at $(x',y')$: the square's horizontal maps are weak equivalences, homotopic realizations have the same weak-equivalence property by the basepoint-change node, and two-out-of-three holds by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] and [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

source.place: Sections 5.3-5.5; mapping-space conjugation argument needed in the proof of Lemma 7.5 (printed p.16).

proof.text: We also record the short cancellation argument for maps of Kan complexes. Suppose $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}T$ have $vu$ and $wv$ weak homotopy equivalences. By [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse], choose simplicial homotopy inverses $r:Z\to X$ of $vu$ and $s:T\to Y$ of $wv$. Put $l=sw:Z\to Y$ and $t=ur:Z\to Y$. Then $lv\simeq1_Y$ and $vt\simeq1_Z$. After realizing, compose these homotopies to obtain $l\simeq lvt\simeq t$, and hence $tv\simeq lv\simeq1_Y$. Together with $vt\simeq1_Z$ this makes $|v|$ a homotopy equivalence. The simplicial homotopies realize using [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder]; [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change] makes $v$ a weak equivalence. Now $vu$ and $v$ give $u$, and $wv$ and $v$ give $w$, by two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] with the axiom in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. This proves the required three-map cancellation for Kan mapping spaces, without any connectedness assumption.

source.place: Lemma 7.5, second clause (printed p.16): explicit Kan-space cancellation underpinning the omitted argument.

proof.text: For ordinary categories, equivalences have the same cancellation property by the definition through quasi-inverses. Write $F=ha$, $G=hb$, $H=hc$. Choose quasi-inverses $L$ to $GF$ and $R$ to $HG$, which exist by the two assumptions. Then $P=RH$ and $Q=FL$ satisfy $PG\cong1_{hA_1}$ and $GQ\cong1_{hA_2}$. Whiskering gives $P\cong PGQ\cong Q$. Therefore also $QG\cong PG\cong1_{hA_1}$, so $Q$ is a quasi-inverse for $G$. It follows that $F\cong QGF$ and $H\cong HGQ$ are equivalences: each displayed right side is a composite of equivalences, whose quasi-inverse is the reverse composite. Thus all three homotopy-category functors are equivalences. In particular $ha$ and $hb$ are essentially surjective. No assertion about the spaces of objects $A_{i,0}$ follows or is needed.

source.place: Lemma 7.5, second clause (printed p.16): ordinary-category part, written using quasi-inverses.

proof.text:
Fix vertices $x,y$ of $A_0$ and consider the maps of Kan spaces
$$M_{A_0}(x,y)\xrightarrow{u}M_{A_1}(ax,ay)\xrightarrow{v}M_{A_2}(bax,bay)\xrightarrow{w}M_{A_3}(cbax,cbay).$$
Here $vu$ is the actual mapping-space map of $ba$ at $(x,y)$, and $wv$ is that of $cb$ at $(ax,ay)$, so both are weak equivalences by hypothesis. Apply the Kan cancellation argument of step 5 (whose inverse maps are furnished by [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse]) to conclude that $u$ and $v$ are weak equivalences. The pair $(x,y)$ was arbitrary, so $a$ is fully faithful on mapping spaces, and $b$ has the same property at every pair $(ax,ay)$. All four spaces are Kan by step 2, so the hypothesis of the inverse theorem is met.

source.place: Lemma 7.5, second clause (printed p.16): cancellation at pairs of objects coming from $A_0$.

proof.text: For any vertices $z,z'$ of $A_1$, essential surjectivity of $ha$ from step 6 supplies vertices $x,y$ of $A_0$ and isomorphisms $ax\cong z$, $ay\cong z'$ in $hA_1$. Use these isomorphisms and their images under $hb$ in the conjugation square of step 4 for the actual map $b$. Its left mapping-space map is a weak equivalence by step 7; its two conjugations are weak equivalences and the square commutes up to realized homotopy. The homotopy-invariance clause of [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change] and the Kan model's two-out-of-three axiom ([lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]) make the right mapping-space map a weak equivalence. This establishes the mapping-space condition for $b$ at every pair, not merely in the image of $a$. Together with step 6, $a$ and $b$ are Dwyer--Kan equivalences.

source.place: Lemma 7.5, second clause (printed p.16): extend full faithfulness of $b$ using essential surjectivity of $ha$.

proof.text:
For vertices $z,z'$ of $A_1$, the composite
$$M_{A_1}(z,z')\xrightarrow{b}M_{A_2}(bz,bz')\xrightarrow{c}M_{A_3}(cbz,cbz')$$
is a weak equivalence by the hypothesis on $cb$, and its first map is a weak equivalence by step 8. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], with its axiom stated in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], makes the second map a weak equivalence. For arbitrary vertices $v,v'$ of $A_2$, essential surjectivity of $hb$ from step 6 gives $bz\cong v$ and $bz'\cong v'$. Apply the step-4 conjugation square to $c$ with those isomorphisms. Its horizontal maps are weak equivalences and its left vertical map is the one just proved to be a weak equivalence; homotopy invariance from [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change] and two-out-of-three give the right vertical map. Thus $c$ is fully faithful on all mapping spaces and, by step 6, is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. This finishes the second clause. Empty Segal spaces and empty mapping spaces require no extra case or nonemptiness assumption: all inverse and lifting statements used allow empty inputs, and the object-pair claims are vacuous when there are no pairs.

source.place: Lemma 7.5, second clause (printed p.16): full faithfulness and conclusion for $c$.
